title: Level 5 (World Class) - A-25
notes:
West leads the ♠10 against 4♥. West's spade lead goes to East's ♠A. East's spade return goes to South's ♠J and is ruffed by West. West gets out with a trump. West's Unusual Notrump overcall and the early play have marked him with 1255 distribution.

The ♣A will take care of 1 of South's diamond losers. As East is known to have only 2 diamonds, his trump will make it impossible to ruff 3 diamonds in the dummy.

South's best chance is to play for an entry shifting trump squeeze. South must try to reach an ending like the above. When South leads the ♥Q, drawing East's last trump, West is squeezed. If West pitches a diamond, South's ♥Q holds. South can now establish a diamond trick by ruffing.

If, instead, West discards a club, North overtakes with the ♥K and a club trick can be set up by ruffing in the closed hand.

For such a squeeze to work, North and South must have an equal number of trumps at the time of the squeeze. The trump suit also must contain the ability to win the squeeze trick in either hand, depending on the defender's choice of discard.

South must win West's heart shift with the ♥A. There are several possible play sequences. South might as well concede a diamond right away. West wins the ♦A and returns a club (he needs to have both the ♣K and ♣Q for the squeeze to function).

The ♣A is won for a diamond discard and a club is ruffed by South. After cashing the ♠K, a diamond is ruffed low in the dummy. Dummy's last spade is ruffed by South. South has achieved a suitable matrix for the entry shifting squeeze. The ♥Q is played leaving West with no answer.
